messages:
acme-devops: Hey team — since last night our services started failing to connect to our Redwood Private endpoint. All clients get `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` and API requests 502/526. Nothing changed on our side other than normal cert sync. Can you help?

maria-support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact TLS error and the domain you're hitting? Also, do you see the error from multiple machines/regions? :eyes: 

acme-devops: domain is `private.acme.internal.redwood` (VPC peering). Error from multiple hosts in the VPC and from our CICD runner. Payload: `Post "https://private.acme.internal.redwood/v1/generate": remote error: tls: handshake failure` and `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`.

aj-ops: Quick check — can you run: `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect private.acme.internal.redwood:443 -servername private.acme.internal.redwood` and paste output? We suspect intermediate chain or SAN ordering mismatch after a rotator job.

acme-devops: pasted below (redacted):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = private.acme.internal.redwood
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify return:1
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF... (leaf)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIJ... (missing intermediate?)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

acme-devops: notice it only returned leaf and a truncated second cert. Our Java clients fail during the chain build.

maria-support: Thanks — that output is helpful. @rotator-bot shows we ran a CA intermediate rotation 8 hours ago (job 1757989000). Does your infra cache cert bundles or pin a CA fingerprint?

rotator-bot: Automated notice: CA rotation completed for private endpoints at 1757989000. New intermediate ID: ii-2026-03-15. Served chain should include leaf + intermediate + root.

aj-ops: Two likely causes: 1) the server (Redwood endpoint) isn't serving the full chain (missing intermediate in TLS handshake), or 2) a middlebox in the VPC is stripping the intermediate. Can you run `curl -vk https://private.acme.internal.redwood/ -o /dev/null` and paste the TLS debug section?

acme-devops: curl shows `* server certificate verification failed.`, and the `* SSL certificate verify result: unable to get local issuer certificate (20)` portion. Also note we have an Envoy sidecar doing TLS termination in front of our callers — we'll check if it's configured to pass through the fullchain.

deepak-se: A couple of repro/debug steps while you check Envoy: 
1) `openssl s_client -showcerts` from outside the VPC (our SRE bastion) — if it shows fullchain, then the issue is inside your network.
2) `openssl x509 -in <certfile> -noout -text` to inspect Authority Information Access (AIA) and OCSP URIs. OCSP egress is required for some clients.

acme-devops: Ran step 1 from SRE bastion: it returns leaf + intermediate + root. So the public-facing load balancer is correct. From inside their VPC it returns only leaf.

aj-ops: That points to an in‑path TLS proxy in your VPC dropping the intermediate or returning a stale cert. Common culprits: internal TLS terminators, API gateways with old bundles, or a caching WAF. Can you search for any iptables NAT or a TLS offload at `10.4.32.14` (your egress gateway)?

acme-devops: Confirmed — we found a corporate proxy at 10.4.32.14 doing TLS MITM for inspection. Its cert bundle hasn't been updated since last year. It validates leaf only and doesn't forward the fullchain.

maria-support: That explains the `unknown authority` message: the proxy presents a different cert chain to your hosts. Two remediation options: 
- Update the proxy's CA bundle to include the Redwood intermediate (preferred), OR
- Configure the proxy to forward TLS passthrough for traffic to `*.redwood`/your internal host so Redwood's endpoint serves the fullchain directly.

deepak-se: Also double-check OCSP/CRL egress allowlists — if the proxy blocks outbound OCSP, clients that validate stapling may fail even with fullchain. Command to test OCSP reachability: `openssl ocsp -issuer intermediate.pem -cert leaf.pem -url http://ocsp.redwood.example` (replace with AIA OCSP URL).

acme-devops: We updated the proxy CA bundle temporarily to include the new intermediate and restarted the proxy. After restart, clients can connect without errors. :tada:

maria-support: Great — thanks for confirming. We'll add a follow-up: infra will add a health-check that verifies fullchain from inside common customer network configurations. @aj-ops can you file an internal ticket to ensure rotator serves fullchain and we monitor for proxies that rewrite chains?

aj-ops: Filing ticket INFRA-3427. Summary: verify TLS endpoints always serve fullchain after rotations; add synthetic checks from common VPC-like NAT paths; alert if s_client from inside network shows missing intermediates.

rotator-bot: Noted. We'll also add an automated Canary that tests handshake from an internal-emu runner.

acme-devops: Thanks all — leaving this open for the INFRA ticket and we'll roll out proxy change to prod. Appreciate fast turnaround.

maria-support: Closing for now since the customer's workaround validated. Reopen if it recurs. :white_check_mark:
